levelMapping: IC3 = Software Engineer (SDE1; 0–2 YOE, India offers ~46–48 LPA total). IC4 = Software Engineer II / 'SDE2' (≈ Google L4 / Amazon SDE II; ~3–5 YOE; India remote offers reported at ~72–74 LPA total in 2025). IC5 = Senior Software Engineer (SDE3; ~5+ YOE, though one 3.5-YOE ex-FAANG SDE2 got IC5 in Feb 2025 at ~1.1 Cr). With ~3.3 YOE target IC4; confirm the level with the recruiter before the loop because the loop content is the same for IC3–IC5 and only the bar differs.

process.summary: Coinbase runs one of the most distinctive loops in the industry: almost no LeetCode-style algorithm puzzles. Instead, every coding round is a 60–90 min 'pair programming' exercise where a deliberately-too-long, multi-stage practical problem (iterators, a bank/ledger, an order-state machine, block mining from a mempool, transaction filters + pagination) is built incrementally in your own editor, with the interviewer grading code quality, OOP/SOLID structure, tests, debugging process and communication as much as correctness. Funnel in 2025–26: recruiter screen → a timed aptitude/cognitive test (40–50 Qs in 15–20 min) plus a 100–200 question personality survey → a 70–90 min CodeSignal 'Industry Coding Framework' OA with one 4-level problem → virtual onsite of 4 rounds: Tech Execution (coding), Domain (coding + design discussion, usually filters/pagination), High-Level System Design (crypto-flavoured), and Hiring Manager/behavioral. In 2026 several loops replaced one coding round with an 'AI-assisted' round (find a bug, design a feature, review an AI-written PR, debug a prod incident while using an AI assistant on screen share). Hiring is decentralized by team; a single 'No Hire' in any onsite round typically ends the loop.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Background, why Coinbase / interest in crypto, experience building APIs, level and comp band, process walkthrough. Recruiters are open about team, stack and comp; one 2024 report says the recruiter previewed the HM-round themes.
rounds.probes: Ownership culture fit, comfort with a mission-focused 'apolitical' workplace, API/backend experience, notice period.

rounds.name: Aptitude + personality assessment (CodeSignal/Criteria style, 'COINsights')
rounds.duration: 15–20 min aptitude (40–50 questions) + untimed ~100–200 question personality survey
rounds.what: Speed-based cognitive test: percentages/basic math, figure-pattern 'odd one out', sentence completion, vocabulary. Then a Likert-scale workstyle survey (Strongly Disagree…Strongly Agree) with repeated questions.
rounds.probes: Expected ~20+/40 correct; most candidates finish 30–35. Keep personality answers consistent across repeated items — automated rejections after this stage are reported and are final.

rounds.name: CodeSignal coding OA (Industry Coding Framework)
rounds.what: ONE problem in 4 incremental levels (~250 pts each); earlier levels' tests keep running as you add features. Themes reported 2024–26: in-memory banking system (create/deposit/transfer → top-k spenders → scheduled payments → merge accounts), cloud file storage (add/get/delete → multi-user capacity → n-largest by prefix / compress → merge users + backup/restore), key-value store with sub-keys/TTL/backup, in-memory DB with TTL + locks, task manager with TTL, versioned recipe store. Variant can depend on the language you pick.
rounds.probes: Need ≥3 of 4 levels (≈440/1000) to advance. Do NOT optimize — brute force passes levels 1–3; design the data model (map of id → object) in level 1 so levels 2–4 are additive. Partial credit per passing test.

rounds.name: Technical phone screen (some pipelines, often US/Canada or referral-led)
rounds.what: One practical build-it problem in your editor: e.g., URL shortener core logic with expiry + concurrent access, mempool block-mining (greedy by fee/size, then child-pays-for-parent), or a k-th element problem. Frontend tracks get an autocomplete component (debounce, async fetch, keyboard nav).
rounds.probes: Clarifying questions, clean working code first try, tests, then scale questions (100k RPS, cross-DC consistency, enumeration safety).

rounds.name: Tech Execution (pair programming #1)
rounds.what: Multi-part (3–5 levels) implementation problem with no starter code and no provided tests, in your own IDE/language on screen share. The classic is the iterator family: interleave n lists → write ListIterator and RangeIterator (start/end/step incl. negative step) with hasNext/next → compose them (interleave a mix of iterators), sometimes a Cycle/Limit/Peek iterator. Other reported prompts: NFT trait-combination generator, food-delivery analytics, event storage with heap/timeout, task-cooldown scheduler, moving-average class, k-th highest leaderboard.
rounds.probes: Edge cases (step==0, invalid ranges, empty lists), SOLID/OOP decomposition, idiomatic naming, writing your own tests, speed — problems are sized to exceed the time; incomplete is OK, sloppy is not. One IC4 reject was for not handling edge cases 'in the first go'.

rounds.name: Domain / Code Design (pair programming #2)
rounds.what: Backend domain problem that is secretly about API design: given transactions {id, time, userId, currency, amount}, implement composable filters (AND of several predicates, =/>/<), then discuss how a UI would fetch a huge result set → pagination strategies (offset vs cursor/keyset) → code cursor-based pagination with limit, filters and nextLink/nextCursor. Variants: order-event stream (NEW/FILL/CANCEL from Kafka) with idempotency, crypto order manager with states, food-delivery top-k queries.
rounds.probes: Why cursor over offset, how to choose the cursor column (stable unique sort key), handling inserts between pages, opaque cursor encoding, thread-safety of a stateful paginator, idempotency keys for at-least-once streams. Running out of time to test the code produced a 'No Hire' in multiple reports.

rounds.name: System design (HLD)
rounds.what: Crypto/fintech-flavoured design: order placement/routing to third-party exchanges (sync-looking API that is really async), crypto price dashboard/ticker aggregating multiple exchanges, stock-broker live prices, notification system with retries/queues, bank ledger, credit-card application, URL shortener, Twitter-style feed.
rounds.probes: Order state machine incl. 'unknown' state after timeout, idempotency/exactly-once ledger application, reconciliation, exchange timeouts and rate limits, spiky traffic/backpressure, fetch frequency vs latency, fan-out to 1B users, observability. Interviewers reward naming a concrete tech you know and admitting uncertainty; confidently-wrong is a negative signal.

rounds.name: AI-assisted coding round (2026 loops, replaces one coding round in some teams)
rounds.what: Given a small codebase (e.g., an in-memory Table with a buggy forward-only Cursor), four stages: find and fix the bug, explain how you would build a new feature (limit/order_by/keyset pagination), review an AI-generated pull request, debug a production incident (duplicate/skipped rows under concurrent writes). You may use an AI assistant; your use of it is recorded and evaluated.
rounds.probes: Whether you read AI output critically, test it against edge cases, justify every accepted line aloud, state the snapshot-vs-live cursor contract and concurrency model.

rounds.name: Hiring Manager / behavioral ('Foundational')
rounds.what: Deep dive on past projects and ownership; STAR questions tied to Coinbase tenets (act like an owner, efficient execution, clear communication, championship team). 2026 HM rounds asked heavily about AI/LLM projects and how you use AI day to day.
rounds.probes: Most complex project and alternatives you considered; a production incident and your role; code you are proud of; when tests can be skipped; disagreement in code review; same problem solved multiple ways; why Coinbase. Expect to be taken deep on any jargon on your CV.

process.indiaNotes: India hiring is fully remote ('Remote - India'; Bengaluru/Hyderabad are where most Indian employees sit but there is no office-based loop). The India loop is identical in structure to the US one (aptitude+personality OA → CodeSignal 4-level OA → 4-round virtual onsite: Tech Execution, Domain, HLD, HM) and uses the same question families; most published 2023–2025 experiences with iterators / transaction-filter pagination / block-mining / bank OA are from Indian IC4/IC5 candidates. IC3 (fresher/PPO) and IC4 (~3–5 YOE) are both hired in India; IC4 India offers ~72–74 LPA total (≈47 L base + ~$27.5k RSU/yr + 5% bonus) in 2025. Recruiters give frequent updates; results in 3–7 days per round. Caveat (Oct 2026): India postings on the careers page are few (7 engineering roles, mostly Senior/Staff, Security Platform, ML) and a Aug-2026 experience mentions layoffs, so confirm active IC4 backend headcount with the recruiter. Older (2021–22) India loops used a Karat screen; that is no longer reported.
process.timeline: Typically 4–8 weeks (Glassdoor average 26 days; Coinbase's own guide says ~60 days). OAs are back-to-back within a week of the recruiter call; onsite rounds are spread over 2–3 days; verdict 3–7 days after the last round. Some candidates report ghosting/no team match after passing all rounds.
tips: Practice in a blank editor with no IDE autocomplete: write an Iterator interface + ListIterator + RangeIterator (negative steps, step==0 error) + an interleaving iterator over a list of iterators, with your own tests, in under 35 minutes in your language.

Model data first: in the CodeSignal OA and pair rounds, start with map<id, Entity> plus an explicit state enum/transition table so levels 2–4 are additive; brute force is fine, speed and passing tests matter more than optimality.
Always write tests and run the code — several 'No Hire' verdicts came from finishing the implementation but having no time to test, or from an untested bug in the last level.

For the Domain round, the hidden theme is pagination: be ready to compare offset vs cursor/keyset, choose a stable (sortKey, id) cursor, encode it opaquely, and code it in 15 minutes after the filters.

Use a high-level language (Python/Java/Go/TS); a candidate was criticised for C++ readability. Follow idiomatic naming and small methods — feedback explicitly cites 'cluttered code', 'redundant classes' and 'poor variable names'.
Clarify AND/OR semantics, tie-breaking, and input format up front — many Coinbase prompts omit I/O format and expect you to define it (one 2026 candidate parsed JSON input themselves).

Know the crypto basics that appear in prompts: mempool, fee/size greedy, child-pays-for-parent (CPFP), order states (NEW/ACTIVE/PAUSED/CANCELLED/FILLED), partial fills, hot vs cold wallets, reconciliation.

For system design, treat any third-party exchange API as async: model order state transitions incl. an 'unknown' post-timeout state, idempotent client order IDs, reconciliation, and backpressure for spiky traffic.
Prepare STAR stories on ownership, a production incident, a code-review disagreement, and how you use AI tools; 2026 HM rounds probe AI/LLM project experience.
Be honest if you have seen a question before — the hiring blog calls out honesty explicitly; most problems are public on LeetCode Discuss/PracHub anyway and interviewers know it.
process.notes: OA platform is CodeSignal (Industry Coding Framework, 4 levels, 70–90 min, proctored with camera/screen recording); earlier years used CodeDrills/HackerRank and a Karat screen. Aptitude test is a CCAT-style 40–50 questions in 15–20 min plus a long personality inventory; automated rejections after it are final and there is a CodeSignal OA cooldown if you take many OAs. No LLD-on-whiteboard round exists — the LLD/OOD evaluation happens inside the pair-programming rounds, which are the core of the loop. Language is your choice but high-level languages are preferred and readability is graded. Decentralized hiring: you may interview with several teams and a strong 'No Hire' in any round ends the process; HM 'soft yes' cannot rescue a 'soft no' coding round. Reports from 2026 mention AI-assisted rounds, Flappy-Bird-style simulation OA problems with an AI helper, and a very tight time budget.

dsa.title: Zigzag / interleaving iterator over n lists
dsa.variant: Level 1 of the Tech Execution iterator problem: given k lists (some empty), e.g. [[1,2,3],[4,5],[6],[],[7,8,9]] → 1,4,6,7,2,5,8,3,9; implemented as a class with hasNext/next, then generalised to accept arbitrary iterator objects (Level 4).
dsa.evidence: Reported in IC4 India offer (2025-02), IC5 offer (2024-05), L5 (2024-10), IC4 reject (2024-06), IC5 onsite (2022-03), Taro Bengaluru (2025-08), PracHub Jul 2025 onsite

dsa.title: Time-based key-value store with sub-keys (CodeSignal OA)
dsa.variant: 4-level OA: set(key, subKey, value, timestamp); get all values for a key; get latest value for (key, subKey); get value at a timestamp; delete key / delete subKey. Another version adds prefix/contains search, optional TTL per key, and backup/restore.
dsa.evidence: IC4 India offer (2025-02); L5 (2024-10); PracHub Nov 2025 DB-design OA

dsa.title: Simple Bank System (CodeSignal OA base)
dsa.variant: OA level 1 is essentially this (create/deposit/withdraw/transfer with validation); levels 2–4 add top-k spenders, scheduled/pending transfers with expiry, cashback, and account merge with history (see lld).
dsa.evidence: CodeSignal OA reports 2023-04, 2024-10, 2025-02, Glassdoor 2026-09 'in-memory banking system'

dsa.title: Design In-Memory File System
dsa.variant: Phone-screen version: mkdir(path), write_file(path, data), read_file(path); OA version is the 'cloud storage' multi-user variant (see lld). Oct 2025 IC4 OA: 'design a file system with multiple follow-ups'.
dsa.evidence: IC4 reject (2025-10) OA; LeetCode phone-screen posts 2021-01, 2022-01

dsa.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Transaction Fee
dsa.variant: Follow-ups: fee charged on both buy and sell; allow holding multiple shares concurrently.
dsa.evidence: PracHub question bank, two entries dated 2025-08 and 2025-09 (onsite)

dsa.title: Top K Frequent Elements over a stream
dsa.variant: Streaming form: insert(item), topk(k) with ties broken lexicographically; follow-ups: sliding window of last T minutes (time buckets), Count-Min Sketch + heap, distributed partition-and-merge. Also framed as 'top-K branches by account openings'.
dsa.evidence: PracHub OA entries 2025-08/09; TechPrep guide cites Top K Frequent

dsa.title: Moving Average from Data Stream (circular buffer)
dsa.variant: Asked as a production-quality class with tests: validate k>0, tests for partial/full window/rollover/k=1/negatives; follow-ups on floating-point drift (periodic recompute) and concurrent next() calls (lock vs lock-free).
dsa.evidence: PracHub onsite report May 2026

dsa.title: Kth largest element in a stream with removals / updates (leaderboard)
dsa.variant: Leaderboard: add score, query current k-th highest, remove user, re-adding a user is an update (must remove the stale score first); ties count separately; return null when fewer than k users. Two ordered sets + user→score map.
dsa.evidence: PracHub onsite May 2026; Taro Canada 'k-th element type problem' Jul 2025

dsa.title: Task scheduler with cooldown, fixed order
dsa.variant: Coinbase variant: tasks must run in the GIVEN order (no rearranging); same type must be ≥ n days apart; idle days allowed; return min days. Track last-run day per task and jump. Follow-ups: n=0, empty list, string IDs, 'where would a maintainer introduce a bug' (the +1).
dsa.evidence: PracHub onsite May 2026

dsa.title: Shortest path to food / collect all items in a grid
dsa.variant: Level 1: BFS from S to one target F. Level 2+: visit ALL F cells (≤12) — BFS over (row, col, mask) or pairwise BFS distances + bitmask DP; the Dec 2025 candidate reached a 5th part that looked like DP.
dsa.evidence: PracHub onsite Dec 2025 (restaurant/food grid), PracHub question bank

dsa.title: Text Justification (modified)
dsa.variant: Asked in the (now-retired) Karat screen as a modification of the LC problem, 45 min.
dsa.evidence: IC4 Karat screen Apr 2022; appears in Coinbase LC tag

dsa.title: Random Pick with Weight / weighted NFT minting with updates
dsa.variant: k NFT types with rarity weights; mint(r) returns the owning index; update(i, delta) changes weights so a static prefix array is O(k) — use Fenwick/segment tree for O(log k) mint+update; follow-ups: mintWithoutReplacement(t), seeded reproducibility, property tests.
dsa.evidence: PracHub onsite entry 2025-09; weighted-rarity follow-up in Feb 2026 IC4 NFT round

dsa.title: Course Schedule II / topological order of transaction dependencies
dsa.variant: Appears inside the block-mining problem: parents must be mined before children; output the lexicographically smallest valid topological order of a selected package; detect cycles.
dsa.evidence: Block-mining CPFP stage reports 2023-04, 2026-04, 2026-05

dsa.title: Currency conversion / best exchange-rate path
dsa.variant: Given exchange rates between currency pairs, convert A→B via intermediate currencies; follow-up: find the most favourable path (max product, log-transform + Dijkstra/Bellman-Ford). Classic Coinbase coding question 2021–2022.
dsa.evidence: IC5 onsite Mar 2022, senior onsite Jan 2022, India Sep 2021

dsa.title: Decode the Message
dsa.variant: OA warm-up level; in LC Coinbase tag.
dsa.evidence: LeetCode Coinbase tag; no 2025–26 narrative report

dsa.title: Design Circular Queue
dsa.variant: Underlies the moving-average class (circular buffer of k values).
dsa.evidence: LeetCode Coinbase tag (recent window); moving-average report 2026-05

dsa.title: Peeking Iterator / composable iterators (peek, take, cycle)
dsa.variant: Follow-up stages of the iterator problem: PeekableIterator with peek()/hasNext(), Cycle iterator that repeats another iterator, Limit iterator that terminates an infinite stream, infinite odd/even iterators where one depends on the other.
dsa.evidence: IC5 onsite 2022-03 (Cycle), 2022-04 help post (Limit/Negative/Interleaving), PracHub composable range iterators 2025-09

dsa.title: Range iterator with step (incl. negative steps)
dsa.statement: Implement RangeIterator(start, end, step) exposing hasNext()/next() that yields start, start+step, … up to and including end when reachable (e.g. 0,10,2 → 0,2,4,6,8,10; 0,-10,-2 → 0,-2,…,-10). Reject step==0 and inconsistent direction (start<end with negative step) explicitly. Must share an interface with a ListIterator so both can be fed to an interleaving iterator.
dsa.variant: Composable library version adds inclusive/exclusive endpoints, overflow-safe termination, map/filter/zip/take/drop/chain combinators in O(1) extra space, reset()/rewind() discussion, iterator invalidation rules.
dsa.evidence: IC4 reject 2024-06, IC4 offer 2025-02, L5 2024-10, PracHub 2025-09

dsa.title: Mempool block mining: maximize fees under block size
dsa.statement: Given a very large unordered mempool of transactions {id, fee, size} and a fixed block size B (=100), implement mine_block(mempool) returning the transactions to include so total size ≤ B and total fee is as high as possible. An exact 0/1 knapsack is explicitly NOT wanted — the interviewer wants a fast heuristic (sort or heap by fee/size ratio, skip what does not fit) with complexity stated and its weak cases discussed.
dsa.variant: Stage 2 adds parent_id (child-pays-for-parent): a child can only be included if its parent is in the same block and placed before it; score ancestor packages as a unit and update scores once ancestors are included; output in topological order; detect cycles. Stage 3 (optional): min_fee(mempool, parent_id, child_size) — the smallest fee a new child must pay so the child+parent package gets into the next block.
dsa.evidence: Reported 2023-04 (IC4 India pair programming), 2026-04 onsite, 2026-05 technical screen, Feb 2026 'passed every round' related question

dsa.title: NFT metadata generator with uniqueness and rarity weights
dsa.statement: Given trait categories each with a list of values (e.g. eyes: blue/green/yellow, hair: black/brown/blue), generate n NFTs that each pick one value per category, guaranteeing no two NFTs share the same full combination; return ERROR if n exceeds the number of distinct combinations (dedupe duplicate values within a category). Output deterministic for a seed. Avoid retry-until-unique sampling — decode distinct indices of the Cartesian product (mixed radix, or a stride coprime to the total).
dsa.variant: Follow-ups: weights per trait value to control rarity (CDF + binary search / Fenwick tree); cap the number of NFTs carrying a given trait value; parse trait definitions from logs first; JSON input the candidate had to define and parse themselves.
dsa.evidence: IC4 India Mar 2024, IC4 Feb 2026 ('many follow-ups, time super tight'), Mar 2026 onsite (levels 1–3)

dsa.title: Flappy Bird jump-boundary function / coin-constrained jump agent (AI-assisted OA)
dsa.statement: Implement one tick of a Flappy-Bird-style simulation: update_bird(y, velocity, jump_pressed, height, gravity, jump_velocity) → (new_y, new_velocity, alive). If jump is pressed set velocity to jump_velocity, then add gravity, then move; alive iff 0 ≤ new_y ≤ height (inclusive). Handle zero gravity and boundary touches. A 2026 OA variant replaces pipes with coins and asks for a stateful jump strategy that collects coins under a resource constraint, with a frontend showing a simulated map and an AI helper available.
dsa.variant: Part of a two-task AI-assisted OA (the other task is block mining with dependencies).
dsa.evidence: PracHub Apr 2026 OA reports (two), question bank Mar–Apr 2026

dsa.title: Order event stream processing with idempotency (NEW / FILL / CANCEL)
dsa.statement: Events {eventId, orderId, type ∈ NEW/FILL/CANCEL, quantity, timestamp} arrive from a Kafka-like at-least-once queue. NEW creates an OPEN order; FILL adds quantity (becomes FILLED when filled == total); CANCEL moves OPEN/PARTIALLY_FILLED to CANCELLED and later fills must be ignored. Part 1: process in order and output per-order state/total/filled. Part 2: duplicates share eventId — only the first occurrence may have an effect so reprocessing yields identical results. Part 3: discuss data structures, transitions and complexity in E events and O orders.
dsa.variant: Dec 2025 candidate was later asked to revisit part 1 — the interviewer wanted idempotency keys considered up front because the source is Kafka.
dsa.evidence: PracHub onsite Dec 2025; question bank Dec 2025

dsa.title: Count users with more than n connections (connect/disconnect stream)
dsa.statement: Process events [userA, userB, 'connect'|'disconnect'] for an undirected graph (repeated connects and disconnects of absent edges are no-ops), then return how many users have degree strictly greater than n. Users exist once they appear.
dsa.evidence: PracHub technical-screen entry Aug 2025

dsa.title: Movie recommendations by shared ratings
dsa.statement: Given rating triplets [user, movie, rating 1–5], recommend to a target user every movie they have not rated that some 'similar' user (one who also rated a common movie 4 or 5) rated 4 or 5; output unique, sorted. Part 2: ratings are a replayable stream too big for an in-memory graph — do it in a few linear passes. Part 3: validate records (malformed, empty names, invalid or conflicting ratings). Part 4: write a checker that flags DUPLICATE / TIE_BREAKING / OFF_BY_ONE bugs in a candidate output.
dsa.evidence: PracHub technical-screen entry Aug 2025

dsa.title: Access-log analysis: per-user access times and most-accessed log in a window
dsa.statement: Given a list of (accessTime, user, logName) entries, return the access times for each user and the log that was accessed most within a given time window. Straightforward hash-map grouping plus windowed counting; graded on clean working code.
dsa.variant: Asked in the (retired) Karat screen for India L5, together with an API-design question.
dsa.evidence: Coinbase L5 India Feb 2022

dsa.title: BTC tax lots: compute realized gains/losses (FIFO cost basis)
dsa.statement: Given a dated list of buy/sell records {date, type, price, amount}, each sell consumes earlier buys (fully or partially) in FIFO order; output for each sale the acquisition date, cost basis, proceeds, gain/loss and amount, and be able to print the remaining open positions (date, amount, cost basis) at any time.
dsa.variant: Follow-up discussion on LIFO/specific-lot selection and floating-point money handling.
dsa.evidence: IC5 phone screen May 2022

dsa.title: Max profit from a list of buy/sell orders
dsa.variant: Given a list of buy and sell orders find the maximum profit a trader can make; followed by open discussion of practical problems a crypto exchange faces.
dsa.evidence: Intern coding round (2021); in Coinbase LC tag

dsa.title: Connect 4 with a basic AI
dsa.statement: Build a playable Connect 4: board, drop-piece move with validation, win detection (4 in a row horizontally/vertically/diagonally), then add a computer opponent — start with random legal moves, then improve (block/win heuristics, minimax). 90-minute pair-programming round judged on structure and tests; a working game with random AI is an acceptable stopping point.
dsa.evidence: India Sep 2021 experience says it was asked multiple times

dsa.title: Find the Length of the Longest Common Prefix
dsa.variant: OA-style; the trie/prefix idea also appears in the key-value store prefixSearch level.
dsa.evidence: LeetCode Coinbase tag only

design.title: Design crypto order placement / routing to third-party exchanges
design.prompt: Design the order-placement system for a crypto trading product: users place, cancel and track buy/sell orders, but Coinbase does not run its own matching engine — orders are routed to one or more external venues with different protocols (REST/WebSocket/FIX) whose APIs look synchronous but whose fills/cancels arrive later.
probes: order state machine incl. an explicit 'unknown' state after a post-send timeout
idempotent submission via client order IDs; accepted-internally vs accepted-by-venue
lost venue ACK but order filled — reconciliation without double-charge
cancelling an order split across two venues with one leg partially filled
exactly-once ledger application of redelivered execution reports
fund reservation/hold model and append-only ledger
exchange timeouts, rate limits, circuit breakers, spiky traffic/backpressure
extension to stop-loss/conditional orders
design.evidence: Reported Jul 2025 (two write-ups), Apr 2026 onsite, 2022 IC6 prep thread ('exchange that only connects to other brokers'), Glassdoor Sep 2026 'Stateful Trading Order Manager'

design.title: Crypto price dashboard / ticker aggregating multiple exchanges
design.prompt: Design a system that pulls price updates for many tokens from several exchanges (e.g. every 2 s) and shows a dashboard with currency name, current/average price and trend, updated every ~10 s, for up to 1B users.
probes: fetch/poll vs streaming frequency per exchange and rate limits
normalisation and aggregation (average/last/top-of-book) per symbol
pub/sub fan-out: WebSocket vs SSE vs long polling; edge caching of current snapshot
minimum-latency display and staleness SLOs
scaling to 1B users: sharding by symbol vs user, multi-region
backpressure/conflation for slow clients
design.evidence: IC5 offer May 2024, L5 Oct 2024, SDE3 India Sep 2024 ('stock broker live prices'), PracHub Jan 2026 'real-time crypto prices homepage', TechPrep 2026

design.title: Design a matching engine for a crypto exchange (high throughput)
design.prompt: Design a high-throughput order-matching engine / order book for a cryptocurrency exchange.
probes: price-time priority data structures (sorted levels + FIFO queues)
single-writer per symbol vs partitioning
determinism, sequencing and replay log
latency vs durability (WAL, snapshots)
market data dissemination and fairness
design.evidence: Glassdoor Aug 2026 (offer); 2022 prep thread 'design a stock exchange'

design.title: Hot and cold wallet architecture for custody of user crypto
design.prompt: Explain how you would design a hot/cold wallet architecture for storing user crypto assets.
probes: key management and HSMs/MPC

lld.title: Custom iterators: interleave n lists → ListIterator + RangeIterator → compose
lld.prompt: Level 1: implement an iterator (hasNext/next) that yields one element from each of n lists in turn, e.g. [[0,1,2],[],[3,4],[5]] → 0,3,5,1,4,2. Level 3: RangeIterator(start, end, step) supporting negative steps and rejecting step 0 / inconsistent direction. Level 4: make the Level-1 class accept any mix of iterator objects (lists and ranges), e.g. [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],Range(1,6,1)] → 1,4,1,2,5,2,3,6,3,4,5,6. Further stages seen: Cycle iterator (repeats another iterator), Limit iterator (terminates an infinite stream), PeekableIterator, infinite odd/even iterators where one depends on the other, a SkipIterator. No starter code and no tests are given.
lld.deliverable: Working, compiling code in your own editor plus your own tests (empty list, single element, exhaustion, next() past end, step==0, negative step)
probes: SOLID/OOP: one interface, small classes, no redundant hierarchy
